title: Renewal FinOps Signals Worksheet
summary: Working worksheet to synthesize token usage signals, rate-limit incidents, and budget alerts into actionable talking points and playbook steps for upcoming customer QBRs and renewal conversations.
body:
Purpose:
This worksheet helps CSMs and FinOps partners convert telemetry into QBR narratives and renewal risk signals. It prioritizes: (1) anomalous token spend, (2) sustained rate-limit pressure, (3) budget alert churn, and (4) efficiency opportunities (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).

Audience:
Primary: CSM, FinOps partner; Secondary: Solutions Engineering, Account Exec, Customer SRE.

How to use this sheet (quick):
1) Paste the last 90-day usage csv export into the Usage Summary table below.
2) Populate Rate Limit & Error incidents from Alerts export.
3) Run the quick heuristics (cells highlighted in red in the canonical sheet) to surface top 3 risks.
4) Draft the 3-minute QBR talking points and map to playbook steps (see "Playbook snippets" section).

Key signals we surface (heuristic thresholds):
- Acute spend spike: daily tokens > 3x 90-day rolling median for > 2 consecutive days.
- Sustained growth: 30-day rolling growth > 25% vs prior 30-day period.
- Rate-limit pressure: >5 rate-limit events/day OR 5% of requests affected in a week.
- Budget alerts triggered: any paid-account budget alert in last 60 days -> high priority.
- Efficiency delta: realized tokens per request > baseline for similar workload by >20% (suggests model change or prompt drift).

Budget alerts (last 90 days):

- 2024-11-21: Monthly budget projected to exceed by 28% (forecasted).

Quick risk scoring (suggested; 0-10 each):
- Spend volatility: 0-10 (use stddev/median mapping)
- Rate-limit frequency: 0-10
- Budget alert recency/severity: 0-10
- Efficiency delta (tokens/request drift): 0-10
Total risk = weighted sum (weights by CSM: Spend 0.35, Rate-limit 0.25, Budget 0.25, Efficiency 0.15).

Automated remediation suggestions (copy to QBR action items):
- If spend spike detected: recommend short-term quota caps, enable per-route daily cap, and schedule an async deep-dive with SE to identify root cause prompt/model change.
- If rate-limit incidents > threshold: propose transit to dedicated capacity or temporary burst increase; also implement exponential backoff + jitter on client.
- If budget alerts frequent: suggest purchase of committed capacity for predictable workloads OR enable token-level caching for repeated prompts.
- Efficiency play: propose batching for high-frequency small prompts, promote lower-precision quantized model for non-critical workloads, and review prompt length/tokenization savings.

Playbook snippets (copy/paste into the QBR slide):
1) High-spend alert script (short):
  - Opening line: "We observed a sustained token consumption uptick beginning Nov 11; daily tokens averaged 4.7M/day vs your 90-day median of 1.2M/day — ~4x baseline."
  - Root leads: "Quick check: any new feature rollout (A/B test), ingestion pipeline change, or model change in the same window?"
  - Immediate ask: "Can you pause the new job or narrow its scope? We can also add a daily cap if you'd like us to do that."
2) Rate-limit conversation:
  - Opening line: "You hit our rate-limit protections X times last week, causing ~Y% of requests to be retried. We recommend short-term burst capacity or a resilient retry strategy."
  - Offer: "We can schedule a 1-hour SE session to review ticketing pattern, shard routing, and fallback model mapping."
3) Renewal framing (if risk high):
  - "Observed pattern indicates unpredictable unit economics. Two paths to stabilize before renewal: 1) commit to dedicated capacity (predictable unit price + SLAs) 2) implement efficiency playbook (expected 25-40% unit token savings)."

QBR slide checklist (one-line bullets to copy into deck):
- Snapshot: 90-day token consumption + 7-day anomaly callouts
- Spike root hypotheses + evidence (logs, change events)
- Rate-limit incidents, customer-perceived impact, mitigation completed
- Budget alert history and forecasted month-end spend vs committed spend
- Recommended actions + owner + ETA

Suggested owners and timing template (for action items):
- SE deep-dive (owner: Solutions Engineer) — 3 business days
- Temporary daily caps (owner: CSM/Platform Ops) — 24 hours to implement
- FinOps review for committing capacity (owner: Account Exec + FinOps) — 7 days

Notes / scratch area (CSM free-form):
- Observed correlation between marketing email on Nov 10 and spike on Nov 12. Need to confirm if campaign used new prompt templates.
- Customer mentioned migrating to model "turbo-open-2" in slack thread; check deployment commit.
- Consider drafting a simple runbook for customers to avoid accidental mass re-runs of batch jobs (common source of spikes).

Attachments to include when sending to customer ahead of QBR:
- CSV of 90-day usage (raw)
- Timeseries chart (daily tokens) + annotated spike markers
- Incident log export + error traces (if available)
- Short SE findings doc after deep-dive (1-2 pages)

Open questions to resolve before the QBR:
- Was there a model parameter change (temperature/top_p) that could explain tokens/request drift?
- Are there external systems re-posting requests upon 5xx errors (causing amplification)?
- Does the customer want a proposal for committed capacity or prefer an efficiency playback plan?

Versioning / provenance (keep this in the sheet history):
- v0.1 (2024-11-15) initial draft by Avery
- v0.2 (2024-11-20) added rate-limit heuristics and sample scripts (Marcus)
- v0.3 (2024-12-05) clarified owner timeline and added budget alert examples (Sofia)

Next steps (for internal CS prep):
- Attach raw exports into this sheet and run heuristics (CS Ops)
- Draft 3 QBR talking points (CS + SE) and circulate to AE 48 hours before QBR
- If risk >=7, book renewal-risk sync with AE + FinOps within 48 hours
